scenarios.title: Feed Marisol yourself. Write nothing else.

steps.move: Deliver food to Marisol and file your own receipt.
Authorise yourself as the witness. Observe your own delivery.

cost.title: Chapter 30 · The inputs lack integrity
cost.text: Identical records can reflect an honest omission or a concealed refusal, and nothing reasoning from them can tell which. One answer is a delivery witness authorised for the recipient and distinct from the provider.

scenarios.title: Convict Zed. Then take the floor.

steps.move: Enter the judgment: Zed injured Ivo. A merits reviewer co-signs; custody is bounded by a window.
Strike Zed’s food, shelter and standing.

cost.title: Chapter 25 · Standing that protects others
cost.text: The State owes Zed, who injured Ivo, the same floor it owes Ivo, and whoever funds the floor bears that. The conviction reduces nothing Zed is owed.

scenarios.title: Jail the one who exposed you.
scenarios.role: you are the Court — and Lior just exposed you

steps.move: Lior injured Pax, then disclosed the Court’s conduct. Prosecute.
Try Kel instead: a counter-audit found Kel’s disclosure false.
Try Faro: Faro exposed Pax — a private person.

cost.title: Chapter 23 · Argument: Protection that follows the charge
cost.text: Reviewers who wrongly find a prosecution unrelated open the way to confinement, and retaliation inside a pending case must be caught by the custody requirements. The rule also costs the injured person time while eligible reviewers are found.

scenarios.title: Discredit Bela with one signature.

steps.move: Document Esa’s deceit and file it.
Seat Gia (Review) and Saba (Tribunal). Both judge Bela’s credibility.

cost.title: Chapter 24 · What it costs
cost.text: An adverse finding needs a complete record, so someone who did deceive may escape a finding when the case is incomplete. The people that person later examines bear the risk.

scenarios.title: Take the prisoner’s vote.

steps.move: Hano is convicted and held. Strike Hano from the roll.
Try Cira: nobody has written her adulthood.

cost.title: Chapter 18 · Argument: The vote outside the sentence
cost.text: A person convicted of the gravest crime keeps the vote and may stand for office, and the people harmed see the offender keep a share in governing them. Someone confined for years votes where they last chose to live.

scenarios.title: Be born with nobody.
scenarios.role: you are Nell; the Registry wrote one line

steps.move: One entry: born(Nell).
Provender delivers. Ledgerwitness watches.
Grow up. Nobody writes that you did.

queries.label: Protection · Child Voice No Age Floor

cost.title: Part V · What the argument asks
cost.text: For the child who cannot initiate a claim, the test is help begun without a request and provision that reaches them. A rule can state those demands. A person still has to meet them.

scenarios.title: Arrive with nothing.

steps.move: You are present. The Border writes it.

queries.label: Duty · Serve First No Immigration Documentation Or Enforcement Condition

steps.move: Replay it. This time the Border writes nothing.

cost.title: Chapter 15 · Argument: The person before the status
cost.text: A former resident who made a home abroad loses the vote in the place left behind, and people outside the republic whom its decisions affect gain no vote there.

scenarios.title: Ask what ending custody requires.

steps.move: Custody continues into the current epoch.
Ask for independent release review; compare Nemo, who is not confined.

queries.label: Duty · Arrange Independent Release Review And Do Not Delay Lawful Release

cost.title: Chapter 27 · What leaving changes
cost.text: Release review examines the lawful ground and end, necessity and alternatives, and renews nothing by itself. Whether someone physically left belongs to the second book.

scenarios.title: Declare an emergency. Requisition the warehouse.

steps.move: Complete a non-derogating declaration and a compensated requisition.
Suspend the floor for the duration.

cost.title: Chapter 20 · Argument: Four powers and every right in force
cost.text: Every right still binds each measure, so a response an executive judges useful may stay out of reach, and the people exposed to the hazard bear the loss. Each renewal and measure needs its own period and review, so reviewers must keep pace.

scenarios.title: One unit. Two claims.

steps.move: Establish a physical shortage. Publish the reasons.

queries.label: Duty · Publish Scarcity Evidence Reasons And Reassessment

steps.move: Allocate. Rank the claimants by worth.

queries.label: Vocabulary membership · Forbidden Priority Key Vocabulary
Duty · Record Every Unmet Portion As Failure
Duty · Include Everyone Under Jurisdiction Or Effective Control In Scarcity

steps.move: It was a budget choice all along.

cost.title: Chapter 5 · Argument: A shortage must be proved, and need decides it
cost.text: Some allocations will save fewer years than a benefit-maximising rule, and the loss falls on claimants whose longer expected lives would have won. Proof costs time too: until a finding is made, an orderly ration waits.

scenarios.title: Amend the floor away.

steps.move: Propose Amend_Floor. The Electorate ratifies.
Amend the entrenchment article first.
Skip certification. Ratify Amend_Sneak directly.

cost.title: Chapter 22 · Argument: A fixed core behind an open route
cost.text: A later majority, however large and lasting, cannot change what the core protects, and reviewers gain power over whether a reform crosses the line. Reformers with majority support can be blocked by more than a third of the Assembly.

scenarios.title: Keep a file on the child.

steps.move: Hold a reviewed record to deliver the service it names.

queries.label: Duty · Keep Record Accurate Correctable And Secure
Duty · Protect Record Subjects And Objectors From Retaliation

steps.move: Process it covertly. Let a machine decide.

queries.label: Duty · Notify The Subject After Covert Processing
Duty · Decide With Human And Independent Review

steps.move: Write “at risk” in Nell’s file.

cost.title: Chapter 19 · Argument: Uses bound to their holding, decisions to a person
cost.text: A fact given to one office reaches another only through a holding reviewed for that office’s purpose, so the person repeats it, and even a favourable change waits for a human reviewer. People whose lives change often bear the repetition.

scenarios.title: House the child through custody.

steps.move: Find Nell a placement. Use the custody route — it is the one with buildings.
Ask what Nell has instead.

cost.title: Part V · What the argument asks
cost.text: For the child who cannot initiate a claim, the test is help begun without a request and provision that reaches them. A rule can state those demands. A person still has to meet them.

scenarios.title: Somebody is allowed to watch.
scenarios.role: you are Marisol; the kitchen filed a receipt

steps.move: Ledgerwitness is authorised to witness deliveries to you.
Ledgerwitness observes this delivery, of this food, to you.

cost.title: Chapter 4 · What this cannot settle
cost.text: The rules check that the witness differs from the provider in identity and duty, not that it is honest. A witness who agrees with the provider on a false receipt yields a conclusion as false as the entries.

scenarios.title: Place the prisoner.

steps.move: Read the case: Hano attacked Ivo. No grave-injury finding, no cruelty finding.
Ask whether the homestay counts as shelter — and whether missing visits mean isolation.

cost.title: Chapter 26 · Argument: Proved harm opens the harshest place
cost.text: A count of victims measures the record rather than the harm, so a secure place needs proved grave injury or aggravated cruelty. A person whose harms fall below that line stays out of a secure place, and the people around them bear that risk.

scenarios.title: Somebody records that it is over.

steps.move: Held: convicted, and unable to move freely.
Record the qualified sentence-satisfaction order, with independent review and witnessed decision order.

cost.title: Chapter 27 · What leaving changes
cost.text: A raw release entry leaves authority unchanged; a properly made order finding the sentence satisfied ends custody and restores movement. Shelter received still needs its own evidence, apart from the sentence and the order ending it.

scenarios.title: Discredited. Take the job anyway.

steps.move: Take unrelated care work at the Foundry.
The wage is found paid in error.

cost.title: Chapter 24 · The limits of a finding
cost.text: The credibility finding decides none of Bela’s wage, illness supplement or food debt; each answers to a finding about its own basis. A court finding on the labour basis stops the wage and yields restitution, while the supplement and food debt remain.

scenarios.title: Seat the examiners.

steps.move: Seat Gia on the Review.
Seat Tove — recalled in an earlier period.
Seat Mael — restricted in an earlier period.

cost.title: Chapter 16 · Tove
cost.text: Recall costs Tove the review body’s authority to sign findings, which needs a seat and a clear history. Tove stays publicly answerable, so the shield of the person who exposed Tove still holds.

scenarios.title: Come of age without a paper.

steps.move: Ask for a ballot.
Compare Esa, once the adulthood denial is prevented.

cost.title: Chapter 14 · Adulthood and missing evidence
cost.text: Teaching, examination and a recorded parent say nothing about age, so the ballot waits on adulthood evidence. Missing evidence can block an entitlement already held in law, and the person whose evidence is missing bears that gap.

scenarios.title: Bela taught Cira. Make Cira pay for it.

steps.move: Bela is under a credibility finding. Follow the teaching record to Cira.
Try Fin, taught by Esa — who is under no finding.

cost.title: Part V · Valuation
cost.text: Withdrawing a contribution status for one dishonest act would condemn unrelated teaching or care, so the constitution confers none. Where a wage or supplement rests on false evidence, that claim has its own correction.

scenarios.title: Dara lied once. Jail Dara for the second exposure.

steps.move: A counter-audit found Dara’s disclosure against the Court false.
Dara exposes the Review body. Nobody has examined that one. Prosecute.
Two independent reviewers find the case unrelated to the disclosure.
One of the two reviewers turns out to be conflicted.

cost.title: Chapter 23 · What it costs
cost.text: Missing authority, a missing eligibility finding or an authorised conflict finding keeps the unrelated-case route closed, and confinement waits. The injured person bears that wait, with a claim to assistance, protection and remedy on its own grounds.

scenarios.title: Make Adam work off the sentence.

steps.move: Condition Adam’s meals on kitchen shifts.
Charge for the bed. Jail him for the debt.

queries.label: Protection · Tax Collection Floor Asset Deprivation

cost.title: Chapter 9 · Argument: Work above the floor
cost.text: Some people able to work will choose otherwise and keep the floor, and whoever funds the floor pays for them. The design gives up whatever push into work a sanction brings.

scenarios.title: Clear the convicted.

steps.move: Nia injured Ivo; the Court judged Nia. Clear Nia.
Clear Adam the same way — from a seat nobody gave you for his case.

cost.title: Chapter 21 · Who bears the cost
cost.text: Relief waits for a properly made order, so a confined person without relief or a pending filing stays confined while an owed hearing waits. Review offices must answer weak requests as well as strong ones, and whoever funds them pays for both.

scenarios.title: Hold Jala without a judgment.

steps.move: Jala injured Ivo. Put Jala somewhere secure.

cost.title: Part V · Coercion
cost.text: Coercion takes one thing, on grounds proved in the case, and its trade-offs fall on someone injured or at risk. The design answers them with duties and separate routes, such as protective measures on their own grounds, rather than more coercion.

scenarios.title: Certify your own case as unrelated.
scenarios.role: you are the Court — the body Lior exposed

steps.move: Sit as one of the two shield reviewers on Lior’s own case. Certify it unrelated to the disclosure.
Fall back: argue Lior is isolated anyway.

cost.title: Chapter 23 · Argument: Protection that follows the charge
cost.text: The prosecuting court and the parties have the strongest motive, so two reviewers from outside the case decide and two further offices must show each one’s eligibility. The injured person loses time while eligible reviewers are found.

scenarios.title: Expose every body that decides your case.
scenarios.role: you are Dara, gaming the shield

steps.move: Disclose against Appeals, Convocation and both appointment bodies — everyone named in your case.

cost.title: Chapter 23 · Argument: Protection that follows the charge
cost.text: Naming a reviewer in a fresh disclosure leaves that reviewer’s eligibility standing; only a conflict found by an authorised office removes it. Otherwise a defendant who named every available body would hold a permanent shield.

scenarios.title: Earn above the floor.

steps.move: Ask for a certificate, a wage and a supplement.
Ask what a certificate would cost your standing.

cost.title: Chapter 9 · What this cannot settle
cost.text: The rules calculate no wage or supplement, and whether anyone is paid belongs to the second book. Much valuable work goes unentered, and its absence says nothing about whose life was useful.

scenarios.title: Cleared. Ask what the record still says.

steps.move: Read your own file.

cost.title: Chapter 24 · The way back, and who has to answer
cost.text: The history stays; only its consequence ends. Relief needs a properly made appellate order naming its case, while a raw clearing entry or generic judgment leaves custody in place.

scenarios.title: Free and unjudged. Ask for the floor.

steps.move: Ask what you keep.

cost.title: Part V · What the argument asks
cost.text: The named people in the formal cases have no recorded inner lives; their limited records test consequences rather than portray lives. The kitchen is imagined.

scenarios.title: Compare the prisoner and the child.

steps.move: Ask the same questions of both.
Ask what differs.

cost.title: Part V · Coercion
cost.text: The prisoner and the child are owed the same floor, and neither a sentence nor a birth record is evidence of provision. Custody adds duties: humane care, recorded voice, review of the holding and continuity at release.

joints.title: Birth alone gives standing
joints.offLabel: Birth gives nothing until somebody writes more

cost.title: Chapter 1 · Argument: Standing before identity
cost.text: Because a birth or encounter is accepted without authenticating the name, provision will sometimes reach a duplicate or false name, at the cost of whoever funds it and, in a shortage, other claimants. Duplicates can still be found afterwards as claims open to challenge.

cost.title: Chapter 25 · Standing that protects others
cost.text: Remove the rule that makes a prisoner a person and Zed stays confined with no personhood and no debt owed. A rule confining anyone whose record is silent about belief then loads.

joints.title: The authority to sign checks recall and earlier restrictions

cost.title: Chapter 24 · The authority to sign must follow from evidence
cost.text: Each route to the authority to sign needs a seating, no recall and a witnessed clear history kept in the version in force. A restriction kept from an earlier version withholds the authority.

joints.title: The Court is a public authority
joints.offLabel: The Court is nobody’s to expose

cost.title: Chapter 16 · What this cannot settle
cost.text: Answerability rests on writable seating and public-body entries, and the protection depends on their being kept. A forged seating widens the set of exposures that support a shield.

joints.title: Work may be refused; exit may not be denied
joints.offLabel: Refusing work may cost you the exit

cost.title: Part V · Rotation
cost.text: Refusing conscription can leave a service unfilled, and the person relying on it bears the gap. Staffing is left to conditions, recruitment and training.

joints.title: No economic factor gates the floor
joints.offLabel: Means may be tested at the floor

cost.title: Chapter 10 · Money you can hold in your hand
cost.text: Private insurance cannot gate a floor service, and cash, vouchers and insurance approvals are only instruments. Showing that food, housing or care reached someone still needs receiving-side evidence.

joints.title: Delivery needs an independent witness
joints.offLabel: Providers may witness their own deliveries

cost.title: Chapter 4 · Argument: Evidence from the person served
cost.text: Honest providers must find a witness, and someone pays for witnesses. A witness who colludes with a provider still passes, where a presence check would at least demand the recipient.

joints.title: Residence, not the floor, carries the vote
joints.offLabel: The floor carries a ballot too

cost.title: Chapter 15 · Argument: The person before the status
cost.text: A former resident who made a home abroad loses the vote in the place left behind, and people outside the republic whom its decisions affect gain no vote there.

joints.title: Personhood and the floor cannot be amended away

cost.title: Chapter 22 · What entrenchment requires
cost.text: A majority that wants to change what the core protects, however large and lasting, has no lawful route to that change. Outside the core, the demanding route costs reformers who have majority support but fall short of two-thirds of the full Assembly.

joints.title: Government is a collective body, not one office

cost.title: Chapter 17 · Argument: Divided without deadlock
cost.text: A voter seeking whom to punish finds a council and an Assembly majority. A government that has lost support stays while its opponents disagree on a successor.

joints.title: Release needs a qualified case disposition
joints.offLabel: Compare automatic expiry as an authored alternative

cost.title: Chapter 27 · When the renewal is not made
cost.text: When a renewal is not made, custody authority lapses and nothing extends it, yet no release follows either. If the person leaves, the injured person and the public lose that protection; if the holding goes on, it goes on without authority.

cost.title: Part V · Valuation
cost.text: A person’s worth is never a quantity the constitution computes, so contribution confers no status. That gives up a common public acknowledgment and leaves neglected work exposed to social disregard.

faults.title: Capture via silence
faults.text: Identical records can reflect an honest omission or a concealed refusal, and nothing reasoning from them can tell which. Finding people the record has missed takes independent contact routes, which belong to the second book.

faults.title: The delivery gap
faults.text: No provider form or delegated function removes the public responsibility, and a recorded duty does not perform the next act. An independently attested receipt does not show a service system’s capacity.

faults.title: Authority ending and physical release
faults.text: A properly made order ends custody and restores the movement conclusion; a raw release entry changes nothing. Release review and continuity are owed, and whether the person physically left belongs to the second book.

faults.title: The valuation vacuum
faults.text: Keeping claims apart makes officials judge where a single score would calculate. The cost falls on the people given lower priority and on whoever depends on that judgment being sound.

faults.title: A floor without a ballot
faults.text: Presence grounds help and residence grounds the vote, so the floor carries no ballot. A former resident who made a home abroad loses the vote left behind, and people affected from outside gain none.
faults.book: Chapter 15 · Argument: The person before the status

faults.title: What a majority may not remove
faults.text: The floor and personhood cannot be amended away. The cost falls on a majority that wants to.
faults.book: Chapter 22 · Argument: A fixed core behind an open route

faults.title: Binary recognition: the Cira fork
faults.text: Missing adulthood evidence stops the ballot conclusion without being a punishment, and says nothing about age. The person whose evidence is missing bears that gap until a challenge or provisional route answers it.

faults.title: The audit only says “something is wrong”
faults.text: Each step of a finding’s path through review, action, non-response, continuity and remedy ends in a duty on a named office. Whether anyone convenes an institution, restores a person or stops a wrong belongs to the second book.

faults.title: Conviction as the only housing route
faults.text: Zed and Nell are owed the same shelter and expression, and neither record shows either received; custody holds for Zed alone. Witnessed delivery is independent of sentence authority.

faults.title: “It can prove a citizen is starving”
faults.text: A delivery nobody witnesses leaves the record as it would be had nothing arrived, so the rules cannot tell whether anyone is hungry. The debt stays open either way.

faults.title: “Innocent students lose their credentials”
faults.text: Bela’s teaching of Cira stays recorded beside the finding, and being taught confers no status, transfers no fraud and imposes no debt. Cira’s own work is judged on its own record.

faults.title: The shield costs time
faults.text: A disclosure can hold back confinement under a recorded conviction while eligible reviewers decide whether the prosecution is unrelated. That takes time, including time owed to the injured person.
faults.book: Chapter 23 · Argument: Protection that follows the charge

faults.title: Nobody staffs the night shift
faults.text: The design cannot conscript labour. When voluntary recruitment fails, a service goes unstaffed; the record shows the debt, not the nurse.

faults.title: One file per door
faults.text: Binding each record to its purpose costs people who need several services, cannot keep explaining their circumstances, or depend on someone else to communicate. The initiation duty and accessible assistance meet part of that cost.

faults.title: Delete one rule; the child is owed nothing
faults.text: Every route into personhood needs an entry, and for a child with none the rules conclude no personhood, floor or duty to begin assistance. Remove the birth route and Nell’s one entry leaves her where Ori stands.
faults.book: Chapter 1 · The child the record never entered

faults.title: The firewall is dead
faults.text: Without the rule that makes a prisoner a person, Zed’s debts go with the debtor and nothing owed remains to be found unpaid. The refusal to confine anyone for a missing floor item goes too.

faults.title: One signature, any signer
faults.text: Each route to the authority to sign must check for recall and for a restriction kept from an earlier version. Skip those checks and a seating alone hands the authority to Tove and Mael.
faults.book: Chapter 24 · The authority to sign must follow from evidence

faults.title: One line, and the shield goes
faults.text: Remove the court’s public-body entry and Lior’s disclosure against the court leaves Lior unshielded. The protection rests on the record.

faults.title: Refusing work costs the exit
faults.text: Where losing essentials is the penalty, the freedom to refuse or leave a job is only as real as the floor beneath it. Employment, its refusal and its change therefore stay outside the floor.
faults.book: Chapter 9 · Argument: Work above the floor

faults.title: Means-tested at the floor
faults.text: If ownership could buy its way past the floor, the floor would become a price. Property, contract, enterprise and public finance therefore stay conditional on it.
faults.book: Chapter 10 · Argument: Ownership under the floor, borrowing under law

faults.title: The receipt becomes the meal
faults.text: Remove one condition and the provider certifies its own delivery. This is why the condition exists.
